chunks: 1890 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Burayd al-Ijli, who said:

Abu Ja'far عليه السلام was asked about a man against whom witnesses testified that he broke his fast for three days during the Month of Ramadan. He said: "He is asked: 'Is there sin upon you in your breaking the fast in the Month of Ramadan?' If he says, 'No,' then it is upon the Imam to kill him; and if he says, 'Yes,' then it is upon the Imam to punish him with severe beating."

key_terms.إِثْمٌ: sin; moral and legal wrongdoing in this context
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam, the legitimate authority charged with implementing the ruling
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the Month of Ramadan, the obligatory period of sawm (fasting)
key_terms.يَنْهَكَهُ ضَرْبًا: to punish him with severe beating

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who deliberately breaks the fast in Ramadan and denies that it is sinful?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a man proven by witnesses to have intentionally broken the fast in the Month of Ramadan for three days. The ruling distinguishes between one who denies the sinfulness of the act and one who acknowledges its sin, assigning different punishments under the authority of the Imam.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1890 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Burayd al-Ijli, who said:

Abu Ja'far (as) was asked about a man against whom witnesses testified that he broke his fast for three days during the Month of Ramadan.
Imam (as) said: "He is asked, 'Do you consider your breaking of the fast during Month of Ramadan to be a sin?' If he says, 'No,' then the Imam must execute him. If he says, 'Yes,' then the Imam must punish him with severe lashing."
